342	- id: cai-isotropy-clusters-2021
343	  title: "Isotropy in the Contextual Embedding Space: Clusters and Manifolds"
344	  authors: [Xingyu Cai, Jiaji Huang, Yuchen Bian, Kenneth Church]
345	  year: 2021
346	  venue: ICLR 2021
347	  url: https://openreview.net/forum?id=xYGNO86OWDH
348	  role: theoretical-foundation
349	  relevance_note: >
350	    ⭐ MOST DIRECTLY RELEVANT. Key insight: global anisotropy is caused by isolated clusters;
351	    WITHIN each cluster, embeddings are locally more isotropic.
352	    Resolution: the high average cosine similarity reported in prior work is an artifact of
353	    mixing embeddings from different clusters — within-cluster geometry is better behaved.
354	    LINK TO OUR WORK: This is the exact mechanism for our "domain boundary" finding.
355	    Cross-domain schemas (ACE vs FewNERD) span DIFFERENT clusters → BCS captures real
356	    inter-cluster distances → proxy works. Same-domain schemas (MAVEN FrameNet types)
357	    fall within ONE cluster → within-cluster variance is low → cosine sim saturates ≥ 0.90
358	    → BCS loses discriminability. Our empirical finding is a direct instantiation of their
359	    theoretical framework applied to type-level (not token-level) embeddings.

363	  authors: [Nathan Godey, Éric de la Clergerie, Benoît Sagot]
364	  year: 2024
365	  venue: EACL 2024
366	  url: https://aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-long.3/
367	  role: theoretical-foundation
368	  relevance_note: >
369	    Proves anisotropy is inherent to the self-attention mechanism itself, not just a
370	    consequence of cross-entropy training on long-tailed token distributions.
371	    Observed across modalities (NLP, vision), ruling out data-distribution explanations.
372	    LINK TO OUR WORK: Strengthens the argument that BCS compression is a fundamental
373	    architectural limitation, not fixable by better prompting or model choice.
374	    Supports our position that structural decomposition (SDGD) is necessary precisely
375	    because the embedding space has inherent geometric constraints.
376	
377	- id: rajaee-cluster-isotropy-2021
378	  title: "A Cluster-based Approach for Improving Isotropy in Contextual Embedding Space"
379	  authors: [Sara Rajaee, Mohammad Taher Pilehvar]
380	  year: 2021
381	  venue: ACL 2021
382	  url: https://aclanthology.org/2021.acl-short.73/
383	  role: theoretical-foundation
384	  relevance_note: >
385	    Shows local (within-cluster) assessment of isotropy is more accurate than global assessment.
386	    Cluster-specific dominant directions encode structural (not semantic) information;
387	    removing them improves semantic task performance.
388	    LINK TO OUR WORK: Supports that within a semantic domain (one cluster), the dominant
389	    directions capture domain-level features rather than fine-grained type distinctions.
390	    This explains why MAVEN type embeddings are compressed: the shared "event-ness"
391	    dominates over type-specific semantics in the local embedding geometry.

402	#    Our multi-channel degradation model (count + confusability + context) is novel.
403	#

405	#    - LLM-PEE (similarity partitioning) — MUST compare
406	#    - PARSE (LLM-driven schema rewriting) — MUST compare
407	#    - DEE (task-level decomposition) — discuss in related work
408	#    - SPT (schema as tools) — discuss in related work
409	#    - DLISC (Dual-LoRA schema caching) — discuss in related work
410	#
411	# 3. "Lost in the Middle" for IE:
412	#    ✅ OPPORTUNITY — No follow-up work applying it to IE task found.
413	#    We can be first to connect positional bias to schema prompt design.
414	#
415	# 4. Multi-agent approaches (CROSSAGENTIE, CMAS):
416	#    Growing area. Position clearly: we reduce confusion proactively via decomposition,
417	#    they resolve it reactively via debate. Complementary, not conflicting.
418	#

420	#    STRONG — no prior work proposes (a) a formal multi-channel degradation model for

422	#    for type confusability. Main risk is CROSSAGENTIE's cross-type debate framing.

    our MAVEN embedding compression is not a Qwen-specific artifact but a general property.

- id: cai-isotropy-clusters-2021

  authors: [Xingyu Cai, Jiaji Huang, Yuchen Bian, Kenneth Church]
  year: 2021
  venue: ICLR 2021
  url: https://openreview.net/forum?id=xYGNO86OWDH
  role: theoretical-foundation
  relevance_note: >

    WITHIN each cluster, embeddings are locally more isotropic.
    Resolution: the high average cosine similarity reported in prior work is an artifact of
    mixing embeddings from different clusters — within-cluster geometry is better behaved.
    LINK TO OUR WORK: This is the exact mechanism for our "domain boundary" finding.
    Cross-domain schemas (ACE vs FewNERD) span DIFFERENT clusters → BCS captures real
    inter-cluster distances → proxy works. Same-domain schemas (MAVEN FrameNet types)
    fall within ONE cluster → within-cluster variance is low → cosine sim saturates ≥ 0.90
    → BCS loses discriminability. Our empirical finding is a direct instantiation of their
    theoretical framework applied to type-level (not token-level) embeddings.

    LINK TO OUR WORK: Strengthens the argument that BCS compression is a fundamental
    architectural limitation, not fixable by better prompting or model choice.
    Supports our position that structural decomposition (SDGD) is necessary precisely
    because the embedding space has inherent geometric constraints.

- id: rajaee-cluster-isotropy-2021

  authors: [Sara Rajaee, Mohammad Taher Pilehvar]
  year: 2021
  venue: ACL 2021
  url: https://aclanthology.org/2021.acl-short.73/

    Cluster-specific dominant directions encode structural (not semantic) information;
    removing them improves semantic task performance.
    LINK TO OUR WORK: Supports that within a semantic domain (one cluster), the dominant
    directions capture domain-level features rather than fine-grained type distinctions.
    This explains why MAVEN type embeddings are compressed: the shared "event-ness"
    dominates over type-specific semantics in the local embedding geometry.

# References Survey for Schema-DAG-Extraction

> Generated: 2026-05-15 | Purpose: Related work expansion (Dream review feedback)

## Required References (14)

### 1. LLM-PEE
- **Full title**: Towards Event Extraction with Massive Types: LLM-based Collaborative Annotation and Partitioning Extraction
- **Authors**: Wenxuan Liu, Zixuan Li, Long Bai, Yuxin Zuo, Daozhu Xu, Xiaolong Jin, Jiafeng Guo, Xueqi Cheng
- **Venue**: EMNLP 2025 (Main)
- **arXiv/DOI**: arXiv:2503.02628 | https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1743/
- **Key contribution**: Proposes similarity-based type recall (ColBERT) + type-partitioning prompting to handle massive event types (3,465 types). Creates EEMT dataset (200K+ samples). Achieves 12.9% F1 improvement over mainstream LLMs in zero-shot setting.
- **Relation to our work**: [support] — Directly validates our core claim that schema partitioning improves LLM IE; their embedding-similarity partitioning is a key baseline for our DAG-based approach.

### 2. GoLLIE
- **Full title**: GoLLIE: Annotation Guidelines improve Zero-Shot Information-Extraction
- **Authors**: Oscar Sainz, Iker García-Ferrero, Rodrigo Agerri, Oier Lopez de Lacalle, German Rigau, Eneko Agirre
- **Venue**: ICLR 2024
- **arXiv/DOI**: arXiv:2310.03668 | https://openreview.net/forum?id=Y3wpuxd7u9
- **Key contribution**: Fine-tunes Code-LLaMA to follow annotation guidelines encoded as Python class definitions with docstrings. Demonstrates that code-style schema representation enables zero-shot generalization to unseen IE tasks.
- **Relation to our work**: [complement] — Demonstrates code-style schema formatting for IE; our work addresses schema complexity/confusability orthogonally to schema representation format.

### 3. GLiNER
- **Full title**: GLiNER: Generalist Model for Named Entity Recognition using Bidirectional Transformer
- **Authors**: Urchade Zaratiana, Nadi Tomeh, Pierre Holat, Thierry Charnois
- **Venue**: NAACL 2024
- **arXiv/DOI**: arXiv:2311.08526 | https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.300/
- **Key contribution**: Compact bidirectional NER model that matches entity type embeddings to span representations in latent space. GLiNER-L (F1=60.9) outperforms ChatGPT and fine-tuned LLMs in zero-shot NER while being 140x smaller than UniNER-13B.
- **Relation to our work**: [contrast] — Encoder-based approach that avoids type confusability via parallel span-type matching; contrasts with our generative decomposition strategy.

### 4. IEPile
- **Full title**: IEPile: Unearthing Large-Scale Schema-Based Information Extraction Corpus
- **Authors**: Honghao Gui, Lin Yuan, Hongbin Ye, Ningyu Zhang, Mengshu Sun, Lei Liang, Huajun Chen
- **Venue**: ACL 2024 (Short)
- **arXiv/DOI**: arXiv:2402.14710 | https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-short.13/
- **Key contribution**: Constructs 0.32B-token bilingual IE instruction corpus with hard-negative schema construction — explicitly building confusable schema pairs to train models to discriminate semantically proximate types. Covers NER, RE, EE across 33 datasets.
- **Relation to our work**: [support] — Hard-negative schema construction directly validates our type confusability hypothesis; their training-based mitigation complements our training-free decomposition approach.

### 5. CrossAgentIE
- **Full title**: CROSSAGENTIE: Cross-Type and Cross-Task Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration for Zero-Shot Information Extraction
- **Authors**: Meng Lu, Yuzhang Xie, Zhenyu Bi, Shuxiang Cao, Xuan Wang
- **Venue**: ACL 2025 Findings
- **arXiv/DOI**: https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.718/ | https://openreview.net/forum?id=OaSBRV0xMG
- **Key contribution**: Multi-agent framework with intra-group cross-type debate (resolves entity-label conflicts via confidence aggregation) and inter-group cross-task debate (NER↔RE mutual refinement). Template fine-tuning distills multi-agent outputs into single model.
- **Relation to our work**: [support] — Explicitly addresses type confusion via multi-agent debate; validates that type confusability is a real bottleneck in zero-shot IE.

### 6. InstructUIE
- **Full title**: InstructUIE: Multi-task Instruction Tuning for Unified Information Extraction
- **Authors**: Xiao Wang, Weikang Zhou, Can Zu, Han Xia, Tianze Chen, Yuansen Zhang, Rui Zheng, Junjie Ye, Qi Zhang, Tao Gui, Jihua Kang, Jingsheng Yang, Siyuan Li, Chunsai Du
- **Venue**: arXiv 2023 (preprint)
- **arXiv/DOI**: arXiv:2304.08085

- **Relation to our work**: [complement] — Representative of instruction-tuning UIE paradigm; our training-free approach targets the same tasks but without fine-tuning.

- **Full title**: KGGen: Extracting Knowledge Graphs from Plain Text with Language Models
- **Authors**: Belinda Mo, Kyssen Yu, Joshua Kazdan, Joan Cabezas, Proud Mpala, Lisa Yu, Chris Cundy, Charilaos Kanatsoulis, Sanmi Koyejo
- **Venue**: NeurIPS 2025

- **Relation to our work**: [complement] — Post-extraction deduplication addresses related but distinct problem; their entity resolution stage handles type/entity confusion at output level vs. our input-level schema decomposition.

- **Full title**: How Contextual are Contextualized Word Representations? Comparing the Geometry of BERT, ELMo, and GPT-2 Embeddings
- **Authors**: Kawin Ethayarajh
- **Venue**: EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019
- **arXiv/DOI**: arXiv:1909.00512 | https://aclanthology.org/D19-1006/
- **Key contribution**: Shows all layers of BERT/ELMo/GPT-2 exhibit anisotropy — representations occupy a narrow cone in embedding space. Upper layers produce more context-specific representations. Less than 5% variance explained by static embeddings.
- **Relation to our work**: [support] — Anisotropy of contextual representations provides theoretical grounding for why embedding-based type similarity measures can be unreliable, motivating our confusability-aware decomposition.

- **Key contribution**: Proves weight-tying in NLG causes word embeddings to degenerate into a narrow cone (especially low-frequency tokens). Proposes cosine regularization (MLE-CosReg) to mitigate.

- **Relation to our work**: [complement] — Positions our work within the broader LLM4IE landscape; our type confusability analysis fills a gap not covered by existing surveys.

- **Authors**: Wenxuan Zhou, Sheng Zhang, Yu Gu, Muhao Chen, Hoifung Poon
